transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you, and thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um... well, I guess what brought me in is... I've been having just a little bit of trouble keeping up at work. I do general maintenance, and lately I keep... well, I keep forgetting scheduled callbacks and work orders. Just basic follow-ups I promised people I'd do. I always mean to do them, I really try to be reliable, you know? But it's just... it's piled up quite a bit. 

To be honest—and I'm a little embarrassed to even admit this—my job is actually the one that sent me here. They told me I need to figure this out before I lose my shot at moving up. I really don't want to let my bosses down, or the people waiting on repairs, so... I hope I'm in the right place for this. Does that make sense as a reason to be here?
Have you noticed these kinds of forgetfulness and trouble staying on task since you were a kid, or is this something that's really only become a problem recently?

Oh, um... well, if I'm being completely honest, which I want to be, because I really want to do this right... I think it's always been there. A little bit, anyway. 

I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm making excuses or anything, but... I do remember being kind of like this back in grade school. Way before I had all this pressure at work. My teachers were always really nice about it, they'd tell my parents I was bright and everything, which was sweet of them. But... I was always the kid who somehow misplaced my homework papers, or I'd only do the first half of the directions because I just... missed the second half somehow. They always had to remind me to actually finish my classwork instead of just staring out the window. 

I always tried my best, I really did, but it was just hard to keep track of everything. I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this, I know it probably sounds like I was just a bad student, but I really wasn't trying to be difficult... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

Growing up and even now, have you also struggled with things like feeling restless, fidgeting a lot, or acting impulsively—like interrupting others or having trouble sitting still—or has your main struggle really just been with focus and forgetfulness?

Oh, no, not really. I mean, I hope I don't come across as restless or anything like that. I've always been pretty quiet, honestly. 

I've never been the type to, you know, jump out of my seat or interrupt people. I really try to be respectful when others are talking, and I don't think I'm impulsive at all. I always try to think things through... even if I end up forgetting what I was thinking about halfway through doing it. 

So, no, I don't think I have any trouble sitting still. It's really just the... the focus part. And the forgetting things. The quiet stuff, I guess you could say. I hope that's alright? I just wouldn't want you to think I was, like, bouncing off the walls or being disruptive or anything.
Over the past few months, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I hope I don't seem like I'm, you know, depressed or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a positive attitude, especially at work. I don't want to be a downer for anyone else. I still really enjoy the things I've always liked doing... well, when I remember to do them, I guess. But no, I haven't been feeling sad or down or anything. I try to just focus on doing my best every day. 

I really hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know I'm struggling with the focus part, but I'm still trying to be happy and keep my chin up. Is that okay?
Can you tell me about your sleep—do you often feel very tired or sleepy during the day, or has anyone mentioned that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing while you sleep?

Oh, um... sleep? No, I don't think I have any problems there. I mean, I hope I'm getting enough rest, I really try to make sure I go to bed at a decent hour so I can be ready for work the next day. 

I definitely don't snore or anything like that—at least, no one has ever told me I do! I'd feel terrible if I was keeping anyone awake. And I don't think I stop breathing, that sounds really scary. 

I do get a little tired during the day sometimes, but I think that's just normal, right? Just from working hard and trying to keep up with everything. I really try not to let it show or slow me down. I just drink a cup of coffee and keep going, because I want to make sure I'm doing a good job. I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm slacking off or sleeping on the job or anything like that.
